clinician.final_diagnosis: emphysematous pyelonephritis complicated by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia
clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient presented with acute-on-chronic pain and urinary retention. An abdominal and pelvic CT scan revealed a prominent left renal staghorn calculus with suspicious intraparenchymal gas locules, leading to a likely diagnosis of emphysematous pyelonephritis. The patient developed tachycardia and fever with early signs of shock, prompting emergent percutaneous nephrostomy tube placement and initiation of broad-spectrum antibiotics, including vancomycin and Zosyn. Post-operatively, a urinalysis and urine culture showed a large amount of blood, positive leukocyte esterase, and an Escherichia coli urinary tract infection. Direct evidence for MRSA bacteremia was not explicitly found in the provided reports.
